at jage.explanation: "At jage" means "to chase" and "to hunt": Politiet jager tyven (The police chase the thief). For animals, it means hunting: Han jager hjorte (He hunts deer).

sentence.da: Hunden vil **jage** katten ud af haven.
sentence.en: The dog wants to chase the cat out of the garden.

at jamre.explanation: "At jamre" means "to wail" or "to whine": to grumble in a sad, drawn-out way, often about small things and as if you feel sorry for yourself: Han jamrer over vejret (He whines about the weather).

sentence.da: Hun bliver ved med at **jamre** over, at det regner.
sentence.en: She keeps whining that it is raining.

at juble.explanation: "At juble" means "to cheer", to shout with joy, often together with others: Folk jubler, når holdet scorer (People cheer when the team scores).

sentence.da: Publikum begynder at **juble**, når sangeren kommer ind.
sentence.en: The audience starts to cheer when the singer comes in.

at justere.explanation: "At justere" means "to adjust", to make a small change so that something becomes exactly right. It fits prices, plans, numbers and machines: Vi justerer planen (We are adjusting the plan).

sentence.da: Mekanikeren vil **justere** bremserne, fordi de er for løse.
sentence.en: The mechanic wants to adjust the brakes because they are too loose.

en jagt.explanation: "En jagt" means "a hunt", chasing wild animals to catch or shoot them. It is also used for any eager search: jagten på en bolig (the hunt for a home). The verb is at jage (to chase).

sentence.da: Mange danskere går på **jagt** efter hjorte om efteråret.
sentence.en: Many Danes go hunting for deer in the fall.

en jakke.explanation: "En jakke" means "a jacket". A thicker, longer one is en frakke (a coat).

sentence.da: Tag din **jakke** på i kulden.
sentence.en: Put your jacket on in the cold.

en japaner.explanation: "En japaner" means "a Japanese person". For things from Japan, use japansk: japansk te (Japanese tea).

sentence.da: Min ven er **japaner**, og han bor i Tokyo.
sentence.en: My friend is Japanese, and he lives in Tokyo.

en jobannonce.explanation: "En jobannonce" means "a job ad", a notice that a company is looking for a new employee. It lists the tasks and what the company wants from you, and it ends with how to get in touch.

sentence.da: I en **jobannonce** står der, hvilke opgaver du skal løse.
sentence.en: A job ad says which tasks you will do.

en jobsamtale.explanation: "En jobsamtale" means "a job interview", a meeting where an employer talks with someone who wants a job.

sentence.da: Jeg har en **jobsamtale** i morgen og er nervøs.
sentence.en: I have a job interview tomorrow and am nervous.

en joke.explanation: "En joke" means "a joke" you tell to make people laugh. To say you are joking, use at lave sjov (to kid around): Jeg laver bare sjov (I am just joking).

sentence.da: Hans **joke** fik os alle til at grine.
sentence.en: His joke made us all laugh.

en jomfru.explanation: "En jomfru" means "a virgin" or "a maiden", a young woman, mostly in old stories and fairy tales. It is also in fixed names: Jomfru Maria (the Virgin Mary), and Jomfruen is the star sign Virgo. Today the word is rare for a living person.

sentence.da: I eventyret redder ridderen den smukke **jomfru** fra tårnet.
sentence.en: In the fairy tale the knight saves the beautiful maiden from the tower.

en jordemoder.explanation: "En jordemoder" means "a midwife", a trained health worker who helps women while they are expecting and when a baby is born. In Denmark most births are led by a jordemoder, and a doctor comes only if there are problems.

sentence.da: En **jordemoder** hjælper kvinden, mens hun føder.
sentence.en: A midwife helps the woman while she gives birth.

en jordnød.explanation: "En jordnød" means "a peanut", built from jord (ground) and nød (nut). It grows under the ground, which explains the name.

sentence.da: Jeg åbner skallen og spiser en **jordnød**.
sentence.en: I open the shell and eat a peanut.

en journal.explanation: "En journal" means "a medical record", the file where a doctor or a hospital writes down your health history. It is also used for a case file at other offices. Do not use it for a diary: that is en dagbog (a diary).

sentence.da: Lægen skriver i din **journal**, hvilken medicin du har fået.
sentence.en: The doctor writes in your medical record which medicine you have gotten.

en journalist.explanation: "En journalist" means "a journalist", someone who reports news for papers, radio or TV.

sentence.da: En **journalist** skriver om nyheder i avisen.
sentence.en: A journalist writes about news in the paper.

en juleferie.explanation: "En juleferie" means "a Christmas vacation", the time off from school or work around Christmas. It is built from jul (Christmas) and ferie (vacation). Ferie also works alone: Jeg har ferie (I am on vacation).

sentence.da: Vi skal have en lang **juleferie** sammen med familien.
sentence.en: We are going to have a long Christmas vacation together with the family.

en julefrokost.explanation: "En julefrokost" means "a Christmas lunch", a big get-together before Christmas with food and drinks. Despite the name, it often starts at noon and runs late into the evening.

sentence.da: Vi har **julefrokost** med kollegerne i december.
sentence.en: We have a Christmas lunch with our coworkers in December.

en julegave.explanation: "En julegave" means "a Christmas present", a gift you give or get at Christmas. It is built from jul (Christmas) and en gave (a gift), which also works alone: Tak for gaven! (Thanks for the gift!)

sentence.da: Under juletræet ligger en **julegave** til dig.
sentence.en: Under the Christmas tree there is a Christmas present for you.

en julemand.explanation: "En julemand" means "a Santa Claus", the man in a red suit who brings gifts at Christmas. It is built from jul (Christmas) and mand (man). The part jul starts many words, such as et julekort (a Christmas card) and en julesang (a Christmas carol).

sentence.da: Far er klædt ud som **julemand** i dag.
sentence.en: Dad is dressed up as Santa Claus today.

en julemiddag.explanation: "En julemiddag" means "a Christmas dinner", the big meal at Christmas. It is built from jul (Christmas) and middag (dinner). Middag is the evening meal: Hvad skal vi have til middag? (What are we having for dinner?)

sentence.da: Vi spiser **julemiddag** hos min mormor.
sentence.en: We eat Christmas dinner at my grandmother's.

en julesang.explanation: "En julesang" means "a Christmas carol", a song that belongs to Christmas. It is built from jul (Christmas) and sang (song), and sang also works as a word on its own: Det er en dejlig sang (That is a lovely song).

sentence.da: Vi synger altid en **julesang** ved juletræet.
sentence.en: We always sing a Christmas carol at the Christmas tree.

en julestjerne.explanation: "En julestjerne" means "a poinsettia", the plant with red leaves that many Danes put in the window before Christmas. It can also mean a star decoration for the tree or the window, so the situation shows which one is meant.

sentence.da: I december står der en rød **julestjerne** i vinduet i stuen.
sentence.en: In December a red poinsettia stands in the living room window.

en jungle.explanation: "En jungle" means "a jungle", the thick, hot tropical land full of plants and trees. It also means a confusing mess: en jungle af regler (a jungle of rules).

sentence.da: Tigeren bor i en tæt **jungle**.
sentence.en: The tiger lives in a dense jungle.

en jurist.explanation: "En jurist" means "a legal professional", someone with a university degree in law. A jurist may work for the state, a company or a union. The word is wider than the English lawyer: a jurist may never argue a case in court. For that job, use en advokat (a lawyer).

sentence.da: Han er uddannet **jurist** og arbejder i et ministerium.
sentence.en: He is a trained legal professional and works in a ministry.

en jury.explanation: "En jury" means "a jury", a group of people who judge something. In Denmark it is used mostly for a talent show or a prize, where the group gives points or picks the winner.

sentence.da: I tv-programmet giver en **jury** point til hver deltager.
sentence.en: In the TV show a jury gives points to each contestant.

en jyde.explanation: "En jyde" means "a Jutlander", a person from the large part of Denmark that is connected to Germany. Their way of speaking is called jysk (Jutlandic), a dialect that can be hard to understand for other Danes.

sentence.da: Min nabo er **jyde** og kommer fra Aalborg.
sentence.en: My neighbor is a Jutlander and comes from Aalborg.

en jæger.explanation: "En jæger" means "a hunter", a person who shoots wild animals, usually in forests and fields. In Denmark, a hunter needs a license called et jagttegn (a hunting license).

sentence.da: En **jæger** skyder hjorte og fasaner i skoven.
sentence.en: A hunter shoots deer and pheasants in the forest.

en jætte.explanation: "En jætte" means "a giant (Norse mythology)". In old Norse stories, jætter are huge beings who live in the wild and are often enemies of the gods. Ancient stone burial chambers are called jættestuer (giants' chambers), because people once believed giants built them.

sentence.da: I de gamle nordiske sagn bor der en **jætte** i bjerget.
sentence.en: In the old Norse legends a giant lives in the mountain.

en jøde.explanation: "En jøde" means "a Jew", a person who belongs to the Jewish people or religion. Danish writes jøde with a small j. The word for Jewish is jødisk.

sentence.da: Min ven er **jøde** og går i synagoge om lørdagen.
sentence.en: My friend is Jewish and goes to synagogue on Saturdays.

et jakkesæt.explanation: "Et jakkesæt" means "a suit", a jacket with matching pants. It is built from jakke (jacket) and sæt (set). Sæt also means a set of things that belong together: et sæt bestik (a set of silverware).

sentence.da: Mange mænd har et **jakkesæt** på til et bryllup.
sentence.en: Many men wear a suit to a wedding.

et job.explanation: "Et job" means "a job", a particular position: Jeg har et nyt job means "I have a new job". Arbejde (work) is the work itself: Jeg skal på arbejde means "I am going to work".

sentence.da: Jeg kan lide mit **job** på kontoret.
sentence.en: I like my job at the office.

et jobcenter.explanation: "Et jobcenter" means "a job center", the public office run by the local council where people without work get help finding a new job and applying for financial support.

sentence.da: Kommunens **jobcenter** hjælper folk uden arbejde med at finde et nyt.
sentence.en: The municipality's job center helps people without work find a new one.

et jordbær.explanation: "Et jordbær" means "a strawberry". It is made of jord (earth, ground) and et bær (a berry). Jord also means soil: Planten står i jord (The plant is in the soil).

sentence.da: Om sommeren spiser vi **jordbær** med fløde.
sentence.en: In the summer we eat strawberries with cream.

et jordskælv.explanation: "Et jordskælv" means "an earthquake". It is built from jord (earth) and skælv (a tremble). At skælve (to tremble) also describes a person: Han skælver af kulde (He trembles from cold).

sentence.da: Husene faldt sammen efter et **jordskælv**.
sentence.en: The houses collapsed after an earthquake.

et jubilæum.explanation: "Et jubilæum" means "an anniversary", a special anniversary of a round number of years, such as 25 or 50, for a company, a club or someone's job. A couple's yearly anniversary is a different word, bryllupsdag (wedding anniversary).

sentence.da: Firmaet fejrer sit 25-års **jubilæum** med en stor fest.
sentence.en: The company is celebrating its 25th anniversary with a big party.

et julesalg.explanation: "Et julesalg" means "a Christmas sale", special offers in shops around Christmas.

sentence.da: I december har mange butikker **julesalg**.
sentence.en: In December, many shops have a Christmas sale.

et juletræ.explanation: "Et juletræ" means "a Christmas tree". It is made of jul (Christmas) and et træ (a tree). Jul also begins other words, such as et julekort (a Christmas card).

sentence.da: Vi pynter et **juletræ** med lys og kugler.
sentence.en: We decorate a Christmas tree with lights and ornaments.

ja.explanation: "Ja" means "yes". Ja, tak means "yes, please" and is the polite way to accept an offer. If a question has ikke (not) in it, like Kommer du ikke? (Aren't you coming?), Danes answer jo (yes) instead of ja.

sentence.da: Vil du have kaffe? **Ja**, tak.
sentence.en: Do you want coffee? Yes, please.

jalousi.explanation: "Jalousi" means "jealousy", the painful feeling when you fear losing someone or want what another person has. Someone who feels it is jaloux (jealous).

sentence.da: **Jalousi** kan ødelægge et godt forhold.
sentence.en: Jealousy can ruin a good relationship.

jaloux.explanation: "Jaloux" means "jealous", fearing that someone may take what you love or want. Say på (of) after it to name the person.

sentence.da: Han er **jaloux** på sin bror.
sentence.en: He is jealous of his brother.

jaloux på.explanation: "Jaloux på" means "jealous of". It can be about wanting what someone has: Jeg er jaloux på din nye bil (I am jealous of your new car). It can also be about love: Han er jaloux på hendes ven (He is jealous of her friend).

forms.da: Hun er jaloux på sin søster.
forms.en: She is jealous of her sister.

sentence.da: Han er **jaloux på** min nye cykel.
sentence.en: He is jealous of my new bike.

jamen.explanation: "Jamen" means "but" or "well" and starts a reply that pushes back a little: Jamen, det passer ikke! (But that is not true!). Jamen, det er jo fint (Well, that is fine) sounds friendly, and the meaning comes from the tone.

sentence.da: **Jamen**, det var slet ikke min idé!
sentence.en: But that was not my idea at all!

januar.explanation: "Januar" means "January". Month names are written with a small letter: midt i januar (in the middle of January).

sentence.da: Det er koldt i **januar**.
sentence.en: It is cold in January.

japan.explanation: "Japan" means "Japan". The J is pronounced like an English Y, so it sounds like YAH-pan.

sentence.da: Sushi kommer fra **Japan**.
sentence.en: Sushi comes from Japan.

japansk.explanation: "Japansk" means "Japanese". It is written with a small letter (japansk), while English Japanese has a capital letter. On its own it is also the name of the language: Jeg taler japansk (I speak Japanese).

sentence.da: Sushi er **japansk** mad.
sentence.en: Sushi is Japanese food.

jaså.explanation: "Jaså" means "is that so" and answers news that you find a little surprising: Jeg har købt en hund. Jaså! (I have bought a dog. Is that so!).

forms.en: Oh, I did not know that.

sentence.da: Du har fået nyt job? **Jaså**, det er flot.
sentence.en: You have a new job? Is that so? That is great.

javel.explanation: "Javel" means "I see" and shows you have heard something, often with a hint of surprise: Jeg er flyttet. Javel (I have moved. I see). A formal, old-fashioned reply is Javel, hr. Hansen (Very well, Mr. Hansen).

sentence.da: Du kommer for sent? **Javel**.
sentence.en: You are coming late? I see.

jazz.explanation: "Jazz" means "jazz", a style of music. Use it with no en or et: Jeg kan godt lide jazz (I like jazz).

sentence.da: Han spiller **jazz** på sin saxofon.
sentence.en: He plays jazz on his saxophone.

jeg.explanation: "Jeg" means "I", and it only has a capital letter at the start of a sentence: Du og jeg (you and I). Compare Jeg ser ham (I see him) with Han ser mig (He sees me): jeg is for the one who does it, mig for the one it happens to.

sentence.da: **Jeg** bor i København.
sentence.en: I live in Copenhagen.

jeg beklager.explanation: "Jeg beklager" means "I'm sorry" in a formal way, used when you apologize for a mistake or a problem, like a delay at work. Among friends, undskyld (sorry) is more common.

sentence.da: Det er min fejl, og **jeg beklager**.
sentence.en: It is my mistake, and I apologize.

jeg er enig.explanation: "Jeg er enig" means "I agree". Enig means "in agreement", so it literally says I am in agreement. To say who you agree with, add med (with): Jeg er enig med dig (I agree with you).

sentence.da: **Jeg er enig** med dig.
sentence.en: I agree with you.

jeg er ked af det.explanation: "Jeg er ked af det" means "I'm sad", and also "I'm sorry" when you regret something. For a quick apology like bumping into someone, undskyld (sorry, excuse me) is more common; jeg er ked af det sounds more heartfelt.

sentence.da: Undskyld, **jeg er ked af det**.
sentence.en: Sorry, I feel bad about it.

jeg er uenig.explanation: "Jeg er uenig" means "I disagree": Jeg er uenig med dig (I disagree with you). Use med (with) for the person and i (in) for the topic: Vi er uenige i det (We disagree about that).

sentence.da: **Jeg er uenig**, men jeg forstår dig.
sentence.en: I disagree, but I understand you.

jeg forstår ikke.explanation: "Jeg forstår ikke" means "I don't understand". Forstår means "understand" and ikke means "not". To say I don't understand it, put det (it) before ikke: Jeg forstår det ikke. To ask for help, add kan du gentage det? (can you repeat that?).

sentence.da: Undskyld, **jeg forstår ikke**.
sentence.en: Sorry, I don't understand.

jeg glæder mig.explanation: "Jeg glæder mig" means "I'm looking forward to it" and is for something good that is coming. Add til to name it: Jeg glæder mig til ferien (I'm looking forward to the vacation).

forms.en: I'm looking forward to the weekend.
We're looking forward to the party.

sentence.da: **Jeg glæder mig** meget til sommeren.
sentence.en: I'm really looking forward to summer.

jeg har det godt.explanation: "Jeg har det godt" means "I'm doing well" and is the usual answer to hvordan har du det? (how are you?). Danish literally says I have it good, so you need det (it); jeg er godt would sound wrong.

sentence.da: Tak, **jeg har det godt**. Og dig?
sentence.en: Thanks, I'm doing well. And you?

jeg har det skidt.explanation: "Jeg har det skidt" means "I'm not doing well" and works for feeling ill as well as feeling down. Skidt means "badly". A milder way to say it is jeg har det ikke så godt (I'm not doing so well).

sentence.da: Jeg er syg. **Jeg har det skidt**.
sentence.en: I am sick. I'm not doing well.

jeg hedder….explanation: "Jeg hedder…" means "my name is…" and you add your name after it. It literally says I am called…, from at hedde (to be called). A common reply is Dejligt at møde dig (Nice to meet you).

forms.da: Hvad hedder du? Jeg hedder Lars.

sentence.da: **Jeg hedder** Anna, og du?
sentence.en: My name is Anna. And you?

jeg kommer fra….explanation: "Jeg kommer fra…" means "I'm from…" and you add a country or town after it. It literally means "I come from…". It answers Hvor kommer du fra? (Where are you from?). For where you live now, say jeg bor i… (I live in…).

sentence.da: **Jeg kommer fra** Canada.
sentence.en: I'm from Canada.

jeg vil gerne have.explanation: "Jeg vil gerne have" means "I would like" and is the polite way to order or ask for something. Put the thing you want after have. Gerne (gladly) makes it sound friendly. Jeg vil have, without gerne, is blunt, like saying I want.

forms.da: Jeg vil gerne have en kaffe.
Jeg vil gerne have to billetter.

sentence.da: **Jeg vil gerne have** en kop te.
sentence.en: I would like a cup of tea.

jer.explanation: "Jer" means "you" when you talk to several people and something is done to them. Compare I er søde (You are all nice) with Jeg kan se jer (I can see you all). For one person, use dig: Jeg kan se dig (I can see you).

sentence.da: Børn, jeg har en gave til **jer**.
sentence.en: Children, I have a gift for you all.

jeres.explanation: "Jeres" means "your" when you talk to several people. Compare din bil (your car, one person) with jeres bil (your car, a group). Jeres stays the same before any word.

sentence.da: Mor og far, er det **jeres** bil?
sentence.en: Mom and Dad, is that your car?

jern.explanation: "Jern" means "iron", the hard metal. It is also a mineral in the body and in food: Spinat indeholder jern (Spinach contains iron). A railway is en jernbane (an iron track), built from jern and bane (track).

sentence.da: Gelænderet er lavet af **jern**.
sentence.en: The railing is made of iron.

jetlag.explanation: "Jetlag" means "jet lag", the tired feeling after a long flight. Danish writes it as one word, while English has two.

forms.en: We got jet lag in Tokyo
How do you get over jet lag?

sentence.da: Efter flyveturen havde jeg **jetlag** i to dage.
sentence.en: After the flight I had jet lag for two days.

jo.explanation: "Jo" has two uses. It means "yes" when you answer a question that has ikke (not) in it: Kommer du ikke? (Aren't you coming?) Jo! (Yes, I am!). Inside a sentence, it adds a feeling like "you know" or "of course", as in det er jo rigtigt (it is, you know, right). For ordinary yes answers, use ja (yes).

sentence.da: Kommer du ikke? **Jo**, jeg kommer!
sentence.en: Aren't you coming? Yes, I am!

jo ... desto.explanation: "Jo ... desto" means "the ... the", for two things that grow together. Jo starts the first part and desto starts the second. After desto and the word with it (hurtigere), the verb comes next: desto hurtigere bliver du (the faster you get).

forms.da: Jo mere du øver, desto bedre bliver du
forms.en: The more you practice, the better you get

sentence.da: Jeg elsker **jo ... desto**: jo mere, desto bedre.
sentence.en: I love jo ... desto: the more, the better.

jord.explanation: "Jord" means "earth" or "soil": the soil that plants grow in, and also the ground you stand on. With a capital letter, Jorden is the planet Earth. For the floor inside a house, Danes say gulv (floor), not jord.

sentence.da: Planter har brug for vand og **jord**.
sentence.en: Plants need water and soil.

jubel.explanation: "En jubel" means "cheering" or "jubilation", the loud joy of many people at once, like a crowd at a concert. It is mostly used without en.

forms.en: There was jubilation in the hall

sentence.da: Efter målet brød der **jubel** ud på tribunen.
sentence.en: After the goal, cheering broke out in the stands.

juice.explanation: "Juice" means "juice". To say what kind, put the fruit in front, as in appelsinjuice (orange juice) or æblejuice (apple juice).

related.en: fruit cordial (a sweet syrup mixed with water)

sentence.da: Man laver **juice** af appelsiner.
sentence.en: You make juice from oranges.

jul.explanation: "Jul" means "Christmas". Compare til jul (at Christmas) with i julen (during the Christmas season). The greeting is Glædelig jul! (Merry Christmas!).

sentence.da: Vi får gaver til **jul**.
sentence.en: We get presents at Christmas.

juleaften.explanation: "Juleaften" means "Christmas Eve". It is built from jul (Christmas) and aften (evening). Use it without en (a) in front: på juleaften (on Christmas Eve).

sentence.da: På **juleaften** pynter vi juletræet og får gaver.
sentence.en: On Christmas Eve we decorate the Christmas tree and get presents.

julepynt.explanation: "Julepynt" means "Christmas decorations". It is built from jul (Christmas) and pynt (decoration), and it stays the same for one or many.

sentence.da: **Julepynt** er kugler og stjerner til juletræet.
sentence.en: Christmas decorations are balls and stars for the Christmas tree.

juli.explanation: "Juli" means "July" and is written with a small letter (juli), while English July has a capital letter. It looks close to juni (June), so check the middle: juli has an l and juni has an n.

sentence.da: Efter juni kommer **juli**.
sentence.en: After June comes July.

juni.explanation: "Juni" means "June" and is written with a small letter (juni), while English June has a capital letter. It looks close to juli (July), so check the middle: juni has an n and juli has an l.

sentence.da: Det er lyst længe i **juni**.
sentence.en: It stays light for a long time in June.

jura.explanation: "Jura" means "law" as a field of study and a profession, not one single law: Hun læser jura på universitetet (She studies law at the university).

sentence.da: Hun læser **jura** for at blive advokat.
sentence.en: She studies law to become a lawyer.

juridisk.explanation: "Juridisk" means "legal" in the sense of law and courts: Det er et juridisk problem, ikke et politisk (It is a legal problem, not a political one). Do not mix it up with lovlig, which means "allowed by law".

sentence.da: En advokat kan give dig **juridisk** hjælp med kontrakten.
sentence.en: A lawyer can give you legal help with the contract.

jysk.explanation: "Jysk" means "Jutlandic", from or about Jylland (Jutland), the part of Denmark that is joined to the rest of Europe. It is also the name of the dialect spoken there.

sentence.da: Min mormor fra Aalborg taler **jysk**.
sentence.en: My grandmother from Aalborg speaks Jutlandic.

jævnligt.explanation: "Jævnligt" means "regularly", again and again with similar gaps, but not on fixed days: Jeg ringer til min mor jævnligt (I call my mother regularly). It comes from jævn (even).

sentence.da: Jeg går **jævnligt** ture for at holde mig i form.
sentence.en: I go for walks regularly to stay in shape.

jødedom.explanation: "Jødedom" means "Judaism", the religion of the Jewish people. Danish writes it with a small letter and often adds -en: I jødedommen hviler man på sabbatten (In Judaism, people rest on the Sabbath).

sentence.da: Han har læst meget om **jødedom** og dens historie.
sentence.en: He has read a lot about Judaism and its history.

jødisk.explanation: "Jødisk" means "Jewish" and describes people, religion and traditions: jødisk mad (Jewish food). A person is en jøde (a Jew), and the religion is jødedom (Judaism).

sentence.da: Min ven er **jødisk** og fejrer Hanukkah i december.
sentence.en: My friend is Jewish and celebrates Hanukkah in December.

jøsses.explanation: "Jøsses" means "gosh", a mild exclamation when something surprises you, sometimes with a little worry or amusement mixed in. It can stand alone or start a sentence.

sentence.da: **Jøsses**, hvor er der mange mennesker her!
sentence.en: Gosh, there are so many people here!
